transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-24
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Priya Shah, Marco Diaz, Ellen Park (Redwood); Rajesh Patel, Lena Gomez, Tom Wu (Aureus Logistics)

Summary:
Quick bridgecall to hand off compliance artifacts after the outage on 2027-03-20 that caused a 23-minute inference degradation for a subset of private deployments. Primary objectives: confirm evidence bundle contents, discuss KV/cache eviction chain, show timeline of rollback and fallbacks, and align on regulator-ready artifacts (SOC2/ISO style).

Topics discussed:
- Postmortem walk-through and timeline
- KV cache eviction and continuous batching impact
- Audit logs, encryption, KMS/HSM evidence
- Chain-of-custody and redaction rules for PII
- Next steps for evidence upload and regulator sign-off

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to keep this tight — 45ish minutes — but got 52 on calendar, so thanks. i'm Priya from Redwood AE, with Marco our SE and Ellen CSM.
[00:00:22] Rajesh Patel: thanks, Priya. stacking in from NYC. um, quick heads up — Tom from security will be leading the evidence checklist on our side.
[00:00:30] Tom Wu: yep, hi. quick note, regulator wants chain of custody for the logs — hash, timestamps, who accessed, et cetera.
[00:00:36] Marco Diaz: understood. we have an evidence bundle draft, includes audit.log, infra events, a compacted kv eviction trace and the canary rollback timeline. some of the filenames might have extra chars — our exporter did that once — so we'll normalize.
[00:00:48] Lena Gomez: can you confirm the retention window for the raw token-level logs? our compliance team says they need 90 days for this class of transactional activity.
[00:00:56] Ellen Park: short answer, we keep full logs for 30 days by default on Hosted, but for Dedicated and Private we can configure retention longer, we have customers on 90+ day retention with archived buckets. we'll include the retention policy in packet.
[00:01:12] Rajesh Patel: okay good. during the incident we saw a pattern: long-tail eviction, increased per-token latency, then a cascade of retries that amplified backpressure. can Marco sketch the timeline?
[00:01:24] Marco Diaz: sure. i'll try — apologies if the auto-transcript messes up some acronyms. so, 03-20 14:07 UTC we saw an initial KV cache pressure event on a subset of nodes in the private cluster — it's a combination of an unbounded prefix expansion in a small customer prompt set and a misapplied cache TTL. that led to memory pressure and then local evictions.
[00:01:48] Marco Diaz: at 14:10 we hit sustained token generation tail latencies, autoscaler engaged, we spun more instances but the continuous batching queue had sticky sessions so there was a small window where some requests were retried. by 14:18 we executed circuit-breaker and failed over to the fallbacks — Redwood Dedicaed fallback (sic) to a smaller quantized model — which restored baseline but introduced mismatch for a tiny percent of responses.
[00:02:07] Tom Wu: can you explain 'sticky sessions' — our infra team uses stateless routing, so curious where stickyness comes from?
[00:02:15] Marco Diaz: yeah, good question. not sticky per HTTP cookie sense — it's the KV cache affinity. when KV shards are hot, requests are routed to keep kv cache warm, so the routing policy keeps them on a subset of nodes. when we scaled, policy interactions meant some requests kept hitting the hot nodes until evictions propagated.
[00:02:32] Rajesh Patel: transcription noise there — the SRE team noted we saw a bunch of EVICT events with similar PID ranges, can you attach those traces?
[00:02:39] Marco Diaz: absolutely, i'll include the raw eviction trace. it's in the draft bundle as kv-eviction-trace-20270320.ndjson but i'll also export a csv for easier reading.
[00:02:47] Lena Gomez: on the KMS side, are the keys rotated during the incident or before? regulator flagged key-rotation timeline as important for forensic evidence.
[00:02:56] Priya Shah: no rotation during the window. our key management log shows rotation 2027-03-01; none on 03-20. we'll include KMS audit events and HSM access logs where applicable.
[00:03:06] Tom Wu: good. how about audit log integrity — can you provide signed hashes or a write-once storage pointer?
[00:03:12] Marco Diaz: yes we can provide SHA256 digests for each log file and a signed attestation from our control plane. for Private deployments we can also drop logs into your own s3-compatible bucket with server-side encryption and provide object-level checksums.
[00:03:25] Rajesh Patel: perfect. for redaction — our legal needs request that we redact PII but keep identifier mapping so we can reconstruct if regulator requests. what's your recommended workflow?
[00:03:33] Ellen Park: we usually provide two tiers: a redacted bundle for general review and a redaction-keyed bundle under stricter NDA for regulator-only requests. we'll add a readme to the evidence bundle that maps the redaction token to the original ID under the stricter access controls.
[00:03:46] Priya Shah: linking to the postmortem doc now — shared doc: https://redwood.app/pm/aureus-2027 (note: internal link, will provide export)
[00:03:55] Rajesh Patel: got it. a few customer questions i want to make sure are covered: SLA impact, timeline to remediation, and whether the fallback could cause semantic regression in responses.
[00:04:06] Marco Diaz: SLA impact: the incident lasted effectively 23 minutes at tail latency; we flagged as sev-2 and applied credit per contract. remediation timeline — short-term we've adjusted the TTL defaults and added tighter eviction thresholds; medium-term is a KV shard rebalancer that we plan to ship in next sprint.
[00:04:23] Marco Diaz: on semantic regression, there is a small delta when we're on quantized fallback models; for deterministic scoring flows we advise re-ranking or run a lightweight post-filter to catch drift. we'll include sample diffs in evidence.
[00:04:37] Lena Gomez: is there any retained artifact that shows which requests hit fallback vs. normal model? we need to correlate customer tickets.
[00:04:44] Marco Diaz: yes, each request logged a model_variant field and a fallback flag. i'll attach a filtered set that shows request IDs, model_variant, and timestamp bucket. note: request IDs are hashed in the redacted bundle.
[00:04:55] Tom Wu: about the chain of custody — does Redwood have a signed attestation template or do we need to generate our own? regulator prefers a vendor-signed attestation.
[00:05:03] Priya Shah: Redwood can provide a vendor attestation — standard format: event list, SHA256 checksums, attestor name, and signature. we'll sign with our code-signing cert and provide contact details for verification.
[00:05:12] Rajesh Patel: can you also include evidence of the canary rollback decision? our audit wants human approvals with timestamps.
[00:05:18] Marco Diaz: we have the canary webhook logs and the operator approval entry in the control plane audit trail — will include a CSV with approver username and epoch time.
[00:05:26] Lena Gomez: great. small nit — we had some confusion in the incident channel about 'KV cache' vs 'K V cache' — the transcript shows both; can you standardize term usage in the readme?
[00:05:34] Marco Diaz: yes, we'll normalize to 'KV cache' and include glossary.
[00:05:38] Ellen Park: quick note on privacy: some of the sample prompt sets contain internal product names; we'll run a redaction pass and give a redaction report.
[00:05:46] Tom Wu: thanks. regulatory ask: provide evidence that encryption in transit was maintained during the event and that no plaintext logs were written to shared storage.
[00:05:55] Marco Diaz: our transmission layer is TLS 1.3; we can provide connection logs and cipher suites used during the window. no plaintext artifacts were written to shared buckets — the exporter writes encrypted objects.
[00:06:05] Rajesh Patel: competitor question — we did some benchmarking with NimbusAI in-house and saw different fallback behavior; are there recommended configs to avoid semantic shifts when falling back?
[00:06:13] Priya Shah: interesting. a couple levers: choose a model_variant that's architecture-compatible (same tokenizer family), tune quantization aggressively only on non-critical paths, and enable re-ranking at the application layer. Marco can run a quick config diff and share recommended settings for your workload.
[00:06:28] Marco Diaz: yes, i'll produce a config delta doc: recommended_model_variants.csv and a small script to compute n-gram regression score.
[00:06:36] Rajesh Patel: timeline for that?
[00:06:38] Marco Diaz: i'll have a draft in 3 business days.
[00:06:41] Priya Shah: ok. let's talk about the packet itself — i'll summarize what's in the compliance bundle so everyone knows expectations.
[00:06:48] Priya Shah: bundle contents: postmortem.pdf (narrative), audit-logs.tar.gz (signed hashes), kv-eviction-trace-20270320.ndjson, canary-approvals.csv, model-variant-map.csv, retention-policy.pdf, redaction-report.pdf, readme.md with glossary and mapping. plus a redacted sample-request-set and an NDA-only mapping bundle.
[00:07:05] Tom Wu: will the postmortem include exact timestamps in both UTC and epoch?
[00:07:09] Priya Shah: yes, both. and we'll annotate the timeline with operator comments where available.
[00:07:14] Lena Gomez: about the 'rebalanced shard' long-term fix — any rough ETA? we prefer to know an approximate sprint estimate for our roadmaps.
[00:07:22] Marco Diaz: the KV shard rebalancer is scoped for the next sprint, aiming for an M1 target, so approximate 4 weeks from now. i'll add more specifics in the delta doc.
[00:07:31] Rajesh Patel: for the incident credits — can someone confirm the SLA hit and credit amount?
[00:07:36] Ellen Park: under your contract clause 4.2 you get a pro-rata credit for sev-2 events of this class; i'll send the invoice credit calculation but high-level it's a single billing period adjustment, we'll follow up in the support ticket.
[00:07:46] Tom Wu: audit question: are your audit logs tamper-evident? can we request a signed timestamp authority timestamp?
[00:07:53] Marco Diaz: yes, we can timestamp the bundle from an external TSA and include that in the bundle.
[00:07:58] Rajesh Patel: excellent.
[00:07:59] Priya Shah: quick interruption — sorry, minor crosstalk — the SRE channel hat —
[00:08:03] (crosstalk)
[00:08:10] Marco Diaz: back on the KV traces — a few of the records might have corrupted utf chars due to exporter quirks; we'll include both raw and cleaned versions and call out the offsets in the readme.
[00:08:23] Tom Wu: curious on the boolean fallback flag — is that emitted synchronously or as a post-hoc audit event?
[00:08:28] Marco Diaz: emitted synchronously per request in the routing meta. it also gets folded into the async audit stream for correlation.
[00:08:35] Lena Gomez: ok. with those items in place we'll try to draft our regulator packet. one ask: can Redwood attest to the absence of data exfil during the window?
[00:08:44] Priya Shah: we can provide network flow logs for the window and show there were no egress spikes to unknown IPs; we'll include those in the evidence bundle.
[00:08:54] Rajesh Patel: perfect. another small request — can we get a non-technical executive summary for our compliance team to include in the regulator packet?
[00:09:02] Ellen Park: yes, we'll produce a 2-page executive summary that explains root cause, impact, remediation, and preventive measures in non-technical language.
[00:09:10] Tom Wu: and put that in PDF with sign-off lines for both parties.
[00:09:14] Priya Shah: yes.
[00:09:16] (pause)
[00:09:20] Marco Diaz: ok, backlog items related to engineering fixes: TTL default clamp, eviction alert tuning, per-shard memory quotas, and the rebalancer. i'll annotate which are hotfix vs. next-sprint.
[00:09:31] Rajesh Patel: can we get a short risk statement re: semantic drift in fallback — for legal, they want a quantified estimate e.g., 'expected <0.5% semantic delta for NLU intents' — do you have a ballpark?
[00:09:41] Marco Diaz: rough ballpark for token-level differences is 0.2–1.2% depending on prompt diversity; for intent-level reranking it's usually <0.5% if you keep same tokenizer family. i'll quantify with sample diffs.
[00:09:56] Lena Gomez: great. last topic: will the evidence bundle be uploaded to a place we control or to Redwood storage? we prefer control for chain-of-custody.
[00:10:05] Priya Shah: we can push to your S3 with object lock enabled, or we can host and provide signed hashes — choice is yours.
[00:10:13] Tom Wu: we want S3 under our control.
[00:10:16] Priya Shah: noted. we'll coordinate with your infra team for credentials and a write policy.
[00:10:21] Rajesh Patel: ok that's for evidence. any open questions from the customer team?
[00:10:26] Tom Wu: one last question — will Redwood mark the postmortem as final or draft? we need a signed final to include with the regulator packet.
[00:10:33] Marco Diaz: we'll publish a draft today and accept one round of comments; then we'll publish final with an author signature and timestamp.
[00:10:41] Ellen Park: i'll drive the comment window; propose 48 hours for comments then finalize.
[00:10:46] Priya Shah: perfect.
[00:10:47] (longer discussion and clarifying questions — transcript samples omitted for brevity)
[00:29:10] Priya Shah: wrapping up — recap of immediate deliverables: 1) postmortem draft export, 2) audit logs with signed hashes, 3) kv eviction traces and csv, 4) canary approval csv, 5) redaction mapping under NDA, 6) executive summary PDF. those will be moved to Aureus S3 bucket.
[00:29:36] Rajesh Patel: sounds good, please include contact for verification if regulator calls.
[00:29:41] Priya Shah: will do — contact: compliance@redwood.ai and I'll cc my manager.
[00:29:46] Marco Diaz: i also logged the engineering issues in our internal tracker and will share the ticket IDs.
[00:29:51] Lena Gomez: rough ETA for the bundle delivery?
[00:29:55] Priya Shah: target is 2027-03-27 EOD for the redacted public bundle, 2027-03-29 for the NDA-protected mapping and full artifacts.
[00:30:02] Tom Wu: noted.
[00:30:05] (wrap and goodbyes)
[00:30:12] Priya Shah: thanks all, appreciate the fast coordination. we'll follow up in the support ticket with links.
[00:30:18] Rajesh Patel: thanks. bye.

Notes & links referenced in call:
- Draft postmortem: https://redwood.app/pm/aureus-2027 (internal)
- Evidence bundle (to be uploaded to Aureus S3): will include audit logs, KV traces, canary approvals, signed checksums
- Support ticket: #56892 (will be updated with links)

End of meeting.
